text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Cabinet to discuss 1997 budget today. Finance Minister Awad says revenues expected to be 1.860 billion dinars against expenditure of 1.837. After foreign grants and loans are removed this will leave a budget deficit of around 2.5 percent of GDP.
- Uzbek Foreign Minister Abdulaziz Komilov arrives in Amman for talks with senior officials on bilateral affairs and Middle East peace.
- Electricity strikes to continue until demands are met. Doctors union discuss pay incentives with health ministry.
- Crown Prince Hassan tells Israeli newspaper the Middle East has become a victim of meaningless cliches like "Peace for Peace" and "Security for Peace".
- Prime Minister Kabariti calls on committee studying implementation of king's amnesty to speed up its work.
- Deputy Prime Minister Ensour says investment inflow into Jordan in first ten months of 1996 grew to 330 million dinars ($466 million), up 25 percent from same period last year.
- Jordan tells UN it is committed to preserving the rights of Palestinian refugees.
- Jordanian officials say Inter-Arab cooperation was given new dimension at the Cairo Middle East economic conference.
